rationale:
Evidence: iteration 8 (kp 2.0, kd 1.5, base_speed 0.9, sensors at y=0.08) is the best design so far at 473.6. Its oval finished in 18 of 20 trials at a mean of 1.91 s, so the course is completable at 0.9 speed with some margin. The s-bend finished in 6 of 20 trials (progress 0.74, 0.6 line-loss events per run). The slalom is the weakest track: progress 0.15, one line-loss event per run, and max_error about 0.063 m just past the 0.06 m off-track floor. Each finished run is worth roughly 900 points, so converting s-bend and slalom runs matters most. Iteration 7 showed that kp 2.4 overshoots on the s-bend, and iteration 8 showed that kd 1.5 helped the s-bend slightly. Sensors are already at the forward limit (y=0.08), and the off-track limit stays at 0.06 m for every allowed body width, so the remaining levers are speed and controller tuning.

Change: base_speed lowered from 0.9 to 0.85, with every other value held at iteration 8. Lateral error in curves grows with speed, and the s-bend and slalom fail by excursion, not by jitter (steering oscillation is 0.17 to 0.37). At 0.85 the oval mean time should rise only to about 2.0 s, still inside the 3 s limit. I am changing one factor, so any result can be attributed to speed. I did not change kp or kd, because iteration 7 showed that raising kp overshoots and the kd 1.5 setting is the best observed.

Expected result: oval completion stays at about 90 percent, with a slightly longer finish time. s-bend finish rate should hold or rise, and slalom progress should move above 0.15. Score target is about 480 to 520. Main risk: the slower speed drops the oval finish rate, or the slalom remains an early-exit failure no matter what the speed is. The revision rounds should check this against the critique.
